verdicts.statement: The Unemployment Insurance program is a federal-state program authorized by federal law.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly describes the UI program as a federal-state program authorized in federal law.

verdicts.statement: State governments set unemployment benefit levels.
verdicts.reason: The context states that states have broad discretion to set benefit levels and that state law establishes benefit levels.

verdicts.statement: State governments set employer contribution levels.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that states have broad discretion to set employer contribution levels.

verdicts.statement: Employer unemployment taxes finance the Unemployment Insurance program.
verdicts.reason: The context states that the program is financed by unemployment tax contributions paid by employers for each covered worker.

verdicts.statement: An unemployment insurance claimant must be able to work to qualify for benefits.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly lists being able to work as a requirement for benefits.

verdicts.statement: An unemployment insurance claimant must seek work to qualify for benefits.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that a claimant must be seeking work to qualify for benefits.

verdicts.statement: An unemployment insurance claimant must be willing to accept suitable work to qualify for benefits.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that a claimant must be willing to accept a suitable job.

verdicts.statement: California allows part-time employees to file unemployment insurance claims.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that California law allows a part-time employee to file a UI claim.

verdicts.statement: Unemployment insurance benefits depend on claimant earnings during the base period.
verdicts.reason: The context states that the amount of benefits available is based on claimant earnings in the base period.

verdicts.statement: California provides a maximum unemployment insurance benefit of $230 weekly for 26 weeks.
verdicts.reason: The context states that the maximum weekly benefit is capped by state law at $230 per week for 26 weeks.

verdicts.statement: An unemployment insurance claimant must report total weekly earnings during weekly certification.
verdicts.reason: The context states that claimants certifying for regular unemployment benefits must report total earnings for the week worked.

verdicts.statement: The greater amount between $25 and 25 percent of wages is not deducted from weekly unemployment insurance benefits.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that the first $25 or 25% of wages, whichever is more, will not be deducted from the benefit amount.

verdicts.statement: Weekly earnings exceeding the exempt amount are deducted from unemployment insurance benefits.
verdicts.reason: The context states that earnings beyond the exempt $25 or 25% of wages will be deducted.

verdicts.statement: Excess earnings during a week may make an unemployment insurance claimant ineligible for benefits during the week.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that earning too much in a week may make a claimant ineligible for benefits that week.

verdicts.statement: Inability to work during a week may make an unemployment insurance claimant ineligible for benefits during the week.
verdicts.reason: The context states that reporting an inability to work when certifying may result in ineligibility for benefits that week.

verdicts.statement: Unavailability for work during a week may make an unemployment insurance claimant ineligible for benefits during the week.
verdicts.reason: The context states that reporting unavailability for work when certifying may result in ineligibility for benefits that week.

verdicts.statement: An unemployment insurance claimant should continue weekly certification for other eligible weeks.
verdicts.reason: The context advises continuing to certify because ineligibility for one week does not preclude eligibility for other weeks.

verdicts.statement: Refusal of suitable work triggers a phone interview.
verdicts.reason: The context states that reporting a refusal of any work during certification requires scheduling a phone interview, which includes suitable work.

verdicts.statement: Refusal of suitable work triggers contact with the employer.
verdicts.reason: The context states that when a claimant reports refusing work, the employer that offered the job will also be contacted.

verdicts.statement: Refusal of suitable work without good cause may affect unemployment insurance eligibility.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that refusing to return to a job or other suitable work without good cause may make a claimant ineligible for benefits.
